mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of housing starts (HOUST) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the correlation between high HOUST levels and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations are revised downwards.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals inflationary pressure and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS increases simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) during a period of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3%) signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 decline and high CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
